To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting us, and I am sorry to hear about your mother’s fall. We would be very pleased to help Margaret settle safely back at home and to welcome her as a new patient.

1. Weekly blister packs

Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs covering seven days, with medications organized into four dosing times each day. There is no charge for the packaging itself; the usual dispensing charges apply. As Margaret is 81, the Ontario Drug Benefit program will generally cover most eligible prescription costs, although any deductible or co-payment will depend on her individual coverage.

2. Pickup and delivery

Margaret’s building is within our free delivery area, which covers addresses within 8 km of the pharmacy. Our regular delivery days are Tuesdays and Fridays, between 2 and 6 pm.

For this first order, we can either hold the packs for pickup on Saturday or arrange a one-off delivery to her home before 1 pm that day. Please let us know which you would prefer.

3. Transferring her prescriptions and preparing the first packs

To arrange the transfer, we will need the name and address of her present pharmacy on Dundas Street and her OHIP number. We will then contact the pharmacy directly; Margaret does not need to sign a transfer form. You can provide these details by calling me.

Please also ask the hospital discharge team to fax all of Margaret’s discharge prescriptions to us early Thursday morning. We need approximately 48 hours to prepare the first packs after receiving everything, including both the hospital prescriptions and the transfers from her previous pharmacy. If we receive the hospital prescriptions early Thursday and the transfer information promptly, we would realistically expect the packs to be ready Saturday.

The first blister packs will not be ready when Margaret leaves hospital on Thursday. Before her discharge, please confirm with the discharge team what interim medication supply she will receive and how she will be helped with every dose until the Saturday pickup or delivery. This is particularly important because several of her medications will be new.

4. Reviewing her medication list

I would be happy to discuss Margaret’s new medication list with you. First, however, we need Margaret’s permission to discuss her medications with you. Our signed Family Communication Consent form records that permission. It protects her privacy and ensures that we share her health information only in the way she wishes.

Margaret can sign the form at the pharmacy, or we can send it with the driver when her medication is delivered. Once it is signed, I can arrange a telephone review with you.

I also recommend a MedsCheck following her hospital discharge. This is an approximately 20-minute, face-to-face medication review. I can provide it at Margaret’s home and could visit on Monday 16 November or Tuesday 17 November after 6 pm. Please let me know whether either evening would suit her.

You can reach me directly at 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, from 9 am to 6 pm.

Thank you for considering our pharmacy. We will do everything we can to make Margaret’s transition home as smooth and well supported as possible.

Sincerely,
Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
